SELECT
  p.customer_id,
  c.first_name,
  c.last_name,
  p.payment_date,
  p.amount
FROM payment p
JOIN customer c ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
views.description:

Required outputs: customer full name (first name and last

Specifically, please determine for which customer and during which month this maximum month-over-month difference occurred, and provide the difference rounded to two decimal places.

SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  p.payment_id,
  p.amount,
  p.payment_date,
  r.rental_id,
  r.rental_date,
  inv.inventory_id,
  inv.film_id,
  c.create_date AS customer_create_date
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN payment p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
LEFT JOIN inventory inv ON inv.inventory_id = r.inventory_id

views.name: chunk_view_0_2
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  actor.actor_id,
  actor.first_name,
  actor.last_name,
  film.film_id,
  film.title,
  -- revenue is not stored in this chunk; include any columns needed to join later (e.g., rental/payment/inventory)
  rental.rental_id,
  rental.rental_date,
  rental.return_date,
  payment.payment_id,
  payment.amount,
  inventory.inventory_id,
  film_actor.last_update        AS film_actor_last_update,
  film.last_update              AS film_last_update
FROM actor
JOIN film_actor ON film_actor.actor_id = actor.actor_id
JOIN film ON film.film_id = film_actor.film_id
LEFT JOIN inventory ON inventory.film_id = film.film_id
LEFT JOIN rental ON rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id
LEFT JOIN payment ON payment.rental_id = rental.rental_id
views.description: Task: For each actor, find their top three films by that film's total revenue, and for each of those films compute the actor's share of the film's revenue by dividing the film's total revenue equally
validated_on: Please find out how widespread the appeal of our top five actors is. What percentage of our customers have rented films featuring these actors?

views.name: chunk_view_0_3

SELECT
  customer.customer_id,
  payment.payment_id,
  payment.payment_date,
  rental.rental_id,
  rental.inventory_id,
  inventory.film_id,
  film.rating,
  payment.amount,
  -- include all payments per customer will be aggregated later; keep payment rows
  customer.create_date,
  customer.store_id
FROM customer
JOIN payment ON payment.customer_id = customer.customer_id
JOIN rental ON rental.rental_id = payment.rental_id
JOIN inventory ON inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
JOIN film ON film.film_id = inventory.film_id

views.body_sql:
SELECT
    s.store_id,
    r.rental_id,
    r.rental_date,
    r.customer_id,
    r.inventory_id,
    r.staff_id,
    st.store_id AS staff_store_id,
    st.staff_id
FROM rental r
JOIN staff st ON r.staff_id = st.staff_id
JOIN store s ON st.store_id = s.store_id
